sentences.text: Crl.P No.7021/2022 is preferred by the petitioners to quash the complaint dated 21.02.2022 and the entire proceedings in Crime No.62/2022 registered at Harohalli Police Station for offences punishable under Section 506, 507 r/w 34 of IPC.
3. Petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 in Crl.P No.564/2022 are present before the Court.
Petitioner No.1 is also the complainant in the connected petition.

They submitted that they have settled the dispute and therefore, they do not want to proceed with the criminal proceedings initiated by them.
NC: 2025:KHC:15332 4.
Both the cases arise out of a matrimonial dispute.

Petitioners in Crl.P No.564/2022 are husband and his family members, wherein respondent No.2/defacto complainant, wife of petitioner No.1 has initiated the said proceeding by lodging a complaint at Subramanyapura Police Station, Bengaluru City registered in Crime No.29/2021.
5.

Petitioners in Crl.P No.7021/2022 are the brother-in-law and father-in-law of respondent No.2/defacto complainant, wherein they challenged the FIR in Crime No.62/2022 registered at Harohalli Police Station, Ramanagara and the consequent proceedings.
6. A Joint affidavit for settlement has been filed and signed by petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 in Crime No.564/2022.
It is stated that pursuant to the settlement agreement, a decree of divorce has been drawn by the family Court, Bengaluru in M.C.No.374/2024 on 26.07.2024.
Hence, the respective complainants have no NC: 2025:KHC:15332 objection to quash both the FIRs and proceedings pending thereon.

7. The joint affidavit reads as under:
"We, (1) Sanjay Kumar Yadav, S/o. Rajendra Yadav, Aged about 30 years, 4/11 KEB Quarters, Yadalam Nagara, Subramanyapura, B'lore-560061 (2) Varsha Kumari D/o Sikandar Prasad, R/at Kurthaul, Patna, Bihar-804453, today at Bangalore do solemnly swear as under:-
1.
We state that, Sanjay Kumar Yadav and his family members are the petitioners in Crl.P.No.564/2022 and Varsha Kumari is the Respondent No.2/Complainant.
The father and brother of Varsha Kumari are the Petitioners in Crl.P.No.7021/2022 and Sanjay Kumar Yadav is the Complainant/Respondent No.2.
2. We state that our marriage was solemnized on 02.03.2020, which due to irreconcilable differences and incompatibility broke down.
3. We state that thereafter complaints in Crime No.29/2021 (CC.No.21107/2021) and Crime No.62/2022 came to be filed which are under challenge in the present petitions.

sentences.text: We state that thereafter, we have entered into Memorandum of Settlement dated 23/07/2024 where in we have agreed to co-operate with each others in quashing the FIRs amongst other terms.
We have been compliant with the terms of the Settlement Agreement and payments therein are made and received.
5. Pursuant to the Settlement Agreement, Divorce Decree dt.26/7/2024 has also been drawn in MC.No.374/2024 and our marriage has been dissolved.

6. Hence in furtherance of the same we have no objections to quash the FIR in Crime No.29/2021 and proceedings in CC.No.21107/2021 on the file of the II ACMM, B'lore and the FIR in Crime No.62/2022 registered before the Harohalli Police Station.
7. That the 'No objection' is being issued on our own volition and there is no coercion.

Wherefore it is most humbly prayed that this Hon'ble Court may kindly be pleased to:-
(i) Quash the proceedings in CC.No.21107/2021 on the file of the II ACMM, B'lore for the offences under Sections 323, 498A, r/w 34 of IPC and Section 3, 4 & 6 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
NC: 2025:KHC:15332 (ii) Quash the complaint dated 21/02/2022 and entire proceedings in Crime No.62/2022 registered by Harohalli Police Station against the Petitioners pending on the file of Prl. Civil Judge & JMFC,
Kanakpura.

In view of the settlement between the parties."
8.

The memorandum of settlement filed by the parties before the VII Additional Senior Civil Judge,
Bengaluru Rural District at Bengaluru in M.C.No.374/2024 is also furnished.

9. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Narinder Singh and Others V. State of Punjab and Another reported in (2014) 6 SCC 466 has held that when the parties have reached the settlement and on that basis,
petition for quashing the criminal proceedings is filed, the guiding factor in such cases would be:(i)
to secure ends of justice; or (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any Court.

- 11 - NC: 2025:KHC:15332 ORDER

Bengaluru pending before the Principal Civil Judge (Jr. Dn) and JMFC Court,
Kanakapura, Ramanagara are quashed.
